rows.description: A toddler flaps hands, bounces and squeals before a treat or outing. Excitement is bodily and contagious, and a big build-up can turn to tears when it ends.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: excitement

rows.description: A toddler widens the eyes, gasps or startles at a sudden sound or pop-up toy. Surprise can turn to laughter or fear depending on trust and the caregiver's calm reaction.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: amusement, fear, surprise, calm

rows.description: A toddler rubs eyes, whines, clings or melts down when overtired. Tiredness is often mistaken for naughtiness, and sleep or rest fixes many tantrums.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: tiredness

rows.subtopic: Visible reactions with multiple possible causes
rows.description: A toddler's tears may mean pain, hunger, fatigue, frustration, fear or joy overload. Caregivers check the body and setting before deciding what the tears mean.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: joy, anger, fear, tiredness

rows.description: A toddler's emotion flashes on quickly and off just as fast, from tantrum to giggle within minutes. Short displays move on with distraction, while lasting ones suggest a need or a health issue.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: amusement

rows.description: A toddler laughs spontaneously at a funny sound, then begins to fake-cry to get attention. The shift to deliberate display marks growing social understanding, and caregivers respond to the need underneath.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: amusement, sadness

rows.description: A toddler cries after a fall and then smiles when comforted, showing relief mixed with distress. Mixed signals are common at this age, and comfort should follow the crying, not the smile.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: sadness, relief

rows.description: A preschooler can usually name happy, sad and angry faces in pictures but confuses similar ones such as fear and surprise. Simple talk about what happened just before the face helps the child read it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: joy, sadness, anger, fear

rows.description: A child in pretend play puts on a scowl or snarl to be a monster while laughing inside. Play faces are posed, so context such as giggling and a playful body tells the audience it is not real anger.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: amusement, playfulness, anger

rows.description: A child pressing lips together to hold back a smile after a mischief or a funny remark is trying to control amusement or pride. It usually shows the child knows the social rule, and it often leaks through the eyes.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: amusement, pride
